title: Refereeing committee delivers verdict on two controversial decisions from Barcelona vs Real Madrid
tweet: CTA ruled Balde’s handball inside Barça’s box was accidental and not a penalty; Cancelo’s challenge on Diomande, while reckless, did not reach the threshold for a red card. Those calls did not alter the 1‑2 loss to Real Madrid.

title: Barcelona identify €70 million-rated Premier League star as potential defensive reinforcement
tweet: Barcelona have earmarked 23‑year‑old Tarik Muharemovic as a defensive option. He has already started every Premier League match for Leeds, and the Bosnian’s valuation could rise beyond €70 million before the 2027 window. As things stand, the club will need to weigh the high price against the risk of missing an urgent short‑term solution.

title: Barcelona youngster sends defiant message after Clasico injury: ‘Only one idea in mind’
tweet: Xavi Espart broke his silence after a right‑ankle syndesmosis injury in the 1‑2 Clasico loss, saying he aims to return stronger. As things stand, the 19‑year‑old will miss about seven weeks, tightening Flick’s already stretched defensive options. The real test is how the coach adjusts without him.

title: Barcelona sounded out Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane over potential move last summer
tweet: Barcelona reached out to Harry Kane last summer after Atlético’s refusal to sell Julian Alvarez. As things stand, Kane’s new contract with Bayern until 2029 rules out a move, forcing Barça to look elsewhere for a centre‑forward.

title: Lamine Yamal breaks silence after Ballon d’Or disappointment: ‘My time will come’
tweet: Lamine Yamal finished third in the 2026 Ballon d’Or, congratulated Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé, and said his priority remains helping Barça lift trophies. The 19‑year‑old declared that his time will come but that the present focus is club success. As things stand, his confidence is steady, but the next Ballon d’Or remains uncertain.

title: The Frenkie de Jong tactical experiment that could take Hansi Flick’s Barcelona to the next level
tweet: Frenkie de Jong’s 96th‑percentile progressive carries show he can carry the ball out of the back and into midfield, a skill that could be used as a right‑back to create a spare man; it would give Rodri space to protect the centre, but the risk of defensive gaps and his recent knee injury make it a tentative, match‑specific experiment.
